claim_text: Journal Technologies says its public court-portal software was targeted by suspicious, malicious automated activity that it first identified on Nov 13
summary: The vendor calls it a “security incident”: “suspicious automated activity” aimed at its public portal technology, first identified Nov 13. Its Nov 20 update calls the activity “malicious attempts.”
detail: This is the company's own wording, on pages we read directly. It is the vendor's account of an attack on its software, not an outside finding. The statements do not say what the activity was trying to do or whether it got in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the vendor's own statements, says it; a news outlet reports the same statement.
notes: The company says portals were targeted. It does not say how many attempts or whether any succeeded.

claim_text: The vendor advised customers to take their public portals offline, and courts did
summary: Journal Technologies says it “advised affected customers to temporarily suspend public portal access” while it investigated. The Kern, Alameda and Marin courts' own notices say their portals are offline for this reason.
detail: Marin County's court notice, read directly on Nov 21, says the vendor told it of “a potential cybersecurity threat” and recommended that all courts suspend access to ePortal and eDelivery “out of an abundance of caution.” The vendor calls the step a precaution.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The vendor and three courts, all Tier 1, describe the same step.

claim_text: Public court portals or e-filing were offline at many courts, including Alameda, Kern, Marin, Ventura, Riverside, Los Angeles, Spokane, Lake County, Illinois, and King County, Washington
summary: Courts in Alameda, Kern, Marin, Riverside, Lake County (Illinois) and King County (Washington) say their portals are offline. LA Superior Court said its reservations and the vendor's e-filing were down. Outlets report Ventura and Spokane.
detail: The outage is of public access to records and filing. Spokane's court says its separate case-management system is not the part that is offline (see c018). In Ventura, criminal and traffic cases use another system that was working normally. Marin says criminal, juvenile and CARE Court filings must be made on paper until its eDelivery service returns. Lake County's circuit clerk said on Nov 20 it was still working with its vendor to restore the portal. King County District Court's Nov 20 order says it shut its e-filing and case access portal on Nov 13 after the vendor urged users to take portals offline; its internal eCourt system is not affected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Six courts' own notices (Tier 1) plus several independent local outlets.
notes: Riverside's court now says its portal is restored (c022).

claim_text: FOX40 also lists Sacramento County and the municipal courts of Las Vegas as affected
summary: FOX40 reports portals unavailable at Sacramento County on Nov 17 and says the outage appears to include the Las Vegas municipal court. It shows a vendor notice on Sacramento County's portal: a restoration time “has not yet been confirmed.”
detail: We did not find a Sacramento or Las Vegas court notice of our own to read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reports it; no court notice for these two was read.
notes: Sacramento and Las Vegas rest on one outlet.

claim_text: FOX40 reports courts in Canada and Australia were also affected; the cause there is not stated
summary: FOX40 says an Alberta appeals court case-management system has been offline since Nov 13 for “unscheduled maintenance” and that a Victoria (Australia) court's case-management system had an “unplanned outage.”
detail: Neither notice names the vendor or a cause in FOX40's report, and we did not read those courts' own pages.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reports it; the Alberta court's own notice confirms the outage but does not tie it to the vendor.
notes: The Alberta court's own notice, read on Nov 21, says its system went offline on Nov 13 for “unscheduled maintenance” and names no vendor or cause. We did not read the Victoria court's page.

claim_text: How many courts and customers are affected is not stated
summary: The vendor says only “many of our customers” and “multiple organizations” and gives no total. The Sacramento Bee counts 20 California superior courts; the Ventura County Star says “dozens of courts.” Other states are affected too.
detail: The vendor serves courts in several states and other countries. No source here gives a count we can verify.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives a total across all states; the Sacramento Bee's count covers California superior courts only (see c019).

claim_text: The vendor says it released a secured software build on Nov 20 that supports the portal version used by about 90% of affected customers
summary: The Nov 20 update says the updated build was tested by its teams and outside security partners and “enables the restoration” of its most widely used public portal technology.
detail: Only the company says this. Nobody outside has tested it. A build being released is not the same as portals being back: each court has to apply it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own statement; no independent check.
notes: Only the company says this. On Nov 18 a company spokesperson told the Sacramento Bee an updated portal had passed an independent security test; no outside party has said so publicly. A build being released is not the same as portals being back: each court has to apply it.

claim_text: The vendor says it found and addressed vulnerabilities; it has not described them
summary: The vendor's statements mention “identified vulnerabilities” and “vulnerability remediation.” A King County, Washington court order says the vendor alerted users on Nov 13 to “a critical vulnerability in its systems.” None names the flaw.
detail: The vendor's own statements, and a court order relaying what the vendor told its customers.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own statements and a court's account of the vendor's Nov 13 alert; the flaws are not described.

claim_text: Kern County's court says its eCourt public portal is offline due to the suspicious activity and gives no estimated restoration time
summary: The Kern court's Online Services page, in an alert dated Nov 20 and read again on Nov 21, says the portal is offline due to “suspicious automated activity” and “There is no ETA at this time.” Its jury portal is not affected.
detail: This is a court's own notice, read directly. It was still up after the vendor's Nov 20 update.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the court's own page, says it.
notes: Correction: earlier versions said the notice had no date. The alert is headed 11/20/2026, the day of the vendor's Nov 20 build.

claim_text: Whether all affected portals are restored is not established
summary: The vendor says restoration timing varies with each customer's setup, and that self-hosted customers must coordinate with its teams. The Nov 20 build covers about 90% of affected customers; the vendor does not say what applies to the rest.
detail: Restoration is court by court. We found no list of courts that are back. Riverside's court said on Nov 18 that it had no confirmed timeline for restoring its public access portal; its Online Services page now says that portal is restored (see c022), the first court restoration we have found. Lake County's circuit clerk in Illinois said on Nov 20, the day of the vendor's build, that it was still working to restore the portal. King County District Court said in its Nov 20 order that it is unclear when public access will be restored. King County's Superior Court Clerk expects its portal to stay down through Nov 29 (see c021).
label: Not established
why_it_supports: One court, Riverside, now says its portal is restored. Others give no date: Kern gives no ETA, Lake County, Illinois, was still restoring Nov 20, and King County, Washington, expects one portal down through Nov 29.

claim_text: Journal Technologies says the tactics resemble those in the FBI's Nov 13 advisory about the ARTEX hacking framework
summary: The Nov 20 update says the activity's automated, “quickly morphing” sequences are “consistent with” tactics in the FBI's Nov 13 advisory on ARTEX, an AI-driven hacking framework copied and used by criminals and state-aligned groups.
detail: This is the vendor's own description, not a finding by the FBI or anyone else. Many actors share tools, and the vendor says an actor can plant misleading clues, so it “can't report with absolute confidence the source.”
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Only the vendor makes the comparison; the FBI document describes ARTEX in general and does not mention this incident.
notes: Resemblance to a tool is not attribution to an actor.

claim_text: Who is behind the activity is not established
summary: The vendor says it cannot report the source with confidence. No government or independent analyst we found names an actor, and we saw no claim of responsibility.
detail: We did not look at leak sites, underground forums or trackers.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source names an actor.

claim_text: Whether any data was exposed is not established
summary: The vendor says it has “found no evidence to date” that Criminal Justice Information (CJI) was exposed and is still validating this. It does not speak to other data, such as civil filings or user accounts.
detail: “No evidence so far” from the company is a statement that the investigation is open, not a finding that nothing was taken.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Only the company speaks to it, and it says the investigation continues.
notes: Illinois's 19th Judicial Circuit relays the vendor as saying no evidence of a data compromise has been found to date; that is the vendor's word passed on, not the court's own finding.

claim_text: Any link to the other outages and incidents reported this week is not established
summary: The Ventura County Star calls this “one of many apparently unconnected incidents nationwide” and lists Microsoft-provided email, air traffic control systems and bank software. No source we read ties this outage to those.
detail: The FBI advisory was published on the same day the vendor saw the activity, but it does not mention this vendor or any court.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source connects them.
notes: Do not tie to other pages on this site without a source.

claim_text: The FBI published an advisory about ARTEX on Nov 13; it does not mention Journal Technologies or any court
summary: FBI FLASH-20261113-001 describes ARTEX as an open-source, AI-driven penetration-testing framework that criminals have used since at least August 2026, and lists mitigations. We read it and found no mention of this vendor.
detail: It is cited here only because the vendor cites it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 government document we read directly.

claim_text: Courts tell people to file in person and to call or visit clerk's offices while the portals are down
summary: Alameda's notice says to file time-sensitive documents in person and to call or visit a clerk's office for case information and tentative rulings. Ventura and Spokane courts are also taking paper filings at the courthouse.
detail: This is the courts' own advice.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Alameda's own notice (Tier 1), with two local outlets reporting the same for their courts.

claim_text: Riverside's court says the outage first disrupted its internal systems and hearings; its internal network was back on Nov 16
summary: MyNewsLA, quoting the court and the District Attorney's office, says the outage first hit all court systems, disrupted hearings and prevented arraignments. The internal network returned Monday morning; the public portal stayed down.
detail: Reported by one outlet from court and prosecutor statements.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet quotes the court and prosecutor; we did not read the court's own page.

claim_text: The vendor says the public portal outage is separate from the court's own case-management system
summary: The company told KHQ the portal and a court's underlying eCourt case-management system are separate, and that the portal outage does not mean the case-management system is offline.
detail: This is the vendor's description, quoted by one outlet. Riverside's experience (c017) shows internal systems were hit there at first.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet quotes the company.

claim_text: The Sacramento Bee reports portals offline at 20 California superior courts, by its own count
summary: The Bee lists Alameda, Amador, Colusa, Del Norte, El Dorado, Fresno, Humboldt, Kern, Kings, Lake, Madera, Nevada, Placer, Riverside, San Benito, Siskiyou, Solano, Tulare and Ventura among them.
detail: The Bee also reports Sacramento's court saying online access to criminal, civil, juvenile, probate, small claims and unlawful detainer case information was affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's own research, published Nov 18; the vendor did not give a count.
notes: Not every court on the list has a notice we read ourselves. The list may have changed since Nov 18 as portals come back.

claim_text: Washoe County's court in Nevada says its case information portal is down with no ETA; its notice does not say why
summary: The Second Judicial District Court's home page, read on Nov 21, says its case information portal “is currently down” and that it does “not have an ETA.”
detail: The court's notice names no vendor or cause. Background-check firms' status pages say the outage is due to the Journal Technologies outage; they are not sources we rely on for that link.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the court's own page, says the portal is down. The link to this vendor is not established by the court.
notes: The notice has no date on it; the time is when we read it. Do not describe Washoe as a confirmed customer affected by this incident without a court or vendor source.

claim_text: King County's Superior Court Clerk in Washington expects its KC Script portal to stay unavailable through Nov 29, citing technical issues at its vendor
summary: The clerk's Nov 20 alert says case search, e-filing, e-service and records requests through the portal are unavailable through Sunday, Nov 29, “due to technical issues experienced by the Court Clerk's vendor.”
detail: The alert does not name the vendor. Westside Seattle reports, citing the court, that the vendor is Journal Technologies. People can file in person at any King County courthouse.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The clerk's own alert (Tier 1) states the outage and expected date. The tie to this vendor rests on one local outlet's reporting.
notes: Treat the vendor link for the Superior Court Clerk as reported, not confirmed, until a court or vendor source names it. King County District Court's own order (s017) does name the vendor.

claim_text: Riverside County's court says its eCourt public access portal has been restored and that all users must reset their passwords
summary: A notice on the Riverside court's Online Services page, read Nov 22, says “Service Restored: eCOURT Public Access Portal” and that all users are required to reset their passwords before signing in.
detail: The notice is undated and does not name the vendor or the cause. It is the same portal the court's Nov 18 release said was down after the vendor's security issue (s016). The court does not say why passwords must be reset; we do not read it as a sign that passwords were taken.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, the court's own page, says it.
notes: The restoration date is not stated on the page.
